robot.name: 1X NEO
robot.status_notes: Preorder home robot: $200 refundable deposit, $20,000 Early Access ownership, or $499/month subscription; first U.S. deliveries claimed for 2026.

currentness.currentness_notes: Treated as purchasable/preorder-current based on official order and factory updates reviewed on 2026-05-16; no verified customer delivery evidence found.

payload.original_value: Arm Payload 18 lbs; Carry 55 lbs; Lift 154 lbs

battery.original_value: 842 Wh; quick charge 6min per hour runtime
battery.notes: Official product/order specs; not independently tested.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Official DoF subtotal from hands 22x2, arms 7x2, neck 3, spine 2, legs 6x2.

walking_speed.original_value: Walking speed 1.4 m/s; max run speed 6.2 m/s

hands.description: Official specs list 22 DoF per hand, hand speed 8.0 m/s, and IP68 submersible hands.

items: Stereo RGB vision used for stair-height inference in 1X mobility controller post

compute.description: Official specs list 1X NEO Cortex using Nvidia Jetson Thor and up to 2070 FP4 TFLOPS; Redwood AI described as a 160M-parameter onboard transformer running around 5 Hz.

actuators.description: Official materials describe 1X Tendon Drive, low-inertia tendon drives, 95% backdrivability, 2% torque accuracy, 1mm accuracy, and soft lattice body/no external pinch points.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Official specs claim 22 DoF per hand and an 18 lb per-arm payload; company AI posts show pick/place and some dexterous task trials, but independent dexterity validation is still absent.
caveats: Official dexterity specs and AI results are not independently measured.
1X's world-model post reports some dexterous tasks remained challenging, including 0% success on drawing and pouring tasks in its displayed chart.
No public long-horizon household manipulation benchmark was found.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: 1X claims NEO works autonomously by default and arrives with basic autonomy, but the product page also discloses scheduled Expert Mode for unknown chores and remote control from the app/VR; media coverage of WSJ hands-on testing stresses heavy teleoperation dependence.
caveats: Autonomy claims are mostly company claims or curated demos.
Expert Mode/remote-control workflow means task completion cannot be credited as fully autonomous unless specifically shown.
No public intervention-rate, fallback-rate, or household task suite benchmark was found.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Official specs claim 1.4 m/s walking and 6.2 m/s max run speed; 1X's mobility post claims omnidirectional walking, sitting, kneeling, floor recovery, and stair traversal using stereo vision.
caveats: Mobility evidence is official/company-run.
No independent stability, fall-rate, stair, or cluttered-home mobility benchmark was found.
Public demo continuity and failure cases were not timestamp-audited in this pass.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Official specs list stereo fisheye cameras, microphones, visual intelligence, memory, and Redwood/World Model perception claims; public evidence remains company-reported rather than benchmarked.
caveats: No independent perception benchmark or raw logs were found.
1X's own world-model post notes remaining weak 3D grounding and real-robot undershoot/overshoot failure modes.
Camera and microphone specs do not prove robust household scene understanding.

human_interaction.summary: Official product materials claim voice interface, built-in LLM, audio intelligence, visual intelligence, memory, ear-ring status indicators, soft body, and no external pinch points.
caveats: Human-interaction claims are not independently safety certified in reviewed sources.
Remote Expert Mode raises privacy and consent concerns that are material for in-home interaction.
No public user-study or accessibility trial data was found.

endurance_reliability.summary: Official specs claim 4h runtime, 842 Wh battery, self-charging, 22 dB audible noise, 2M nominal tendon-drive load cycles, and factory reliability testing at 20M+ cycles and counting.
caveats: Runtime, noise, and load-cycle claims are official and not independently tested.
No public field uptime, warranty return, maintenance, or MTBF data was found.
Factory reliability lab claims do not equal home deployment reliability.

human_environment_fit.summary: NEO is explicitly positioned for homes, with bipedal mobility, stairs, soft washable suit/shoes, soft body, no external pinch points, 5'6" height, and 66 lb weight.
caveats: Home fit is primarily design intent and company demo evidence.
Reviewed media still emphasizes unknown behavior when the robot gets stuck, falls, or encounters ordinary home edge cases.
No independent in-home trial report with success/failure rates was found.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Official order page supports $200 refundable deposits, $20,000 Early Access ownership, $499/month subscription, and U.S. deliveries starting 2026; 1X says 10,000 NEOs booked out next-year production capacity in five days and Hayward full-scale production has commenced.
caveats: Preorders and factory capacity are not the same as completed customer deployments.
No independently verified customer delivery, installed-base, or retention data was found.
Production-capacity claims are company claims.

accessibility_value.summary: NEO is marketed as a home helper/companion with voice interface, mobile app, scheduled chores, and remote Expert assistance, which could be valuable for some users if reliability and privacy constraints are solved.
caveats: No accessibility-specific trials, caregiver studies, or independent user outcomes were found.
Remote operation and in-home camera/microphone use may be disqualifying for some users.
Do not credit broad accessibility value beyond stated design intent.

evidence_items.title: Official NEO hardware and availability specs
evidence_items.claim: 1X's product/order pages list NEO as a 5'6", 66 lb bipedal home robot with 22 DoF per hand, 18 lb arm payload, 55 lb carry, 154 lb lift, 1.4 m/s walking speed, 842 Wh battery, 4h runtime, Nvidia Jetson Thor compute, dual stereo fisheye cameras, $20,000 Early Access ownership, and $499/month subscription.
evidence_items.notes: Official source; specs and pricing are authoritative for claimed product configuration but not independently measured.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Establishes product identity, home form factor, claimed physical capability envelope, and preorder commercial posture.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Official pages list height 5'6", weight 66 lbs, lift 154 lbs, carry 55 lbs, arm payload 18 lbs, hands 22x2 DoF, walking speed 1.4 m/s, battery 842 Wh, runtime 4h, chipset 1X NEO Cortex (Nvidia Jetson Thor), dual 8.85MP 90Hz stereo fisheye cameras, $20,000 ownership, and $499/mo subscription.
evidence_items.source_location: NEO product page Hardware section and Order page pricing/spec sections
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company-published specifications and order terms; no independent measurements or shipment confirmation.

evidence_items.title: Hands-on/media reporting emphasized teleoperation dependence
evidence_items.claim: WSJ hands-on coverage, summarized by reputable media and linked in the existing audit, reported that NEO's demonstrated work was heavily dependent on Expert Mode / human teleoperation rather than mature autonomy.
evidence_items.notes: Use as a major autonomy caveat. It is hands-on/media context, not a controlled benchmark.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Prevents over-crediting chore demos or preorder claims as autonomous household capability.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Media coverage of the WSJ hands-on said the robot required human teleoperation for launch-era task completion and highlighted privacy concerns around remote operators seeing through NEO's cameras.
evidence_items.source_location: I Tried the Robot That’s Coming to Live With You. It’s Still Part Human; Tom's Guide coverage of WSJ hands-on test
evidence_items.verification_notes: Source-backed but scoped to reported hands-on context; no full raw benchmark data.

evidence_items.title: Official Expert Mode and remote-control disclosure
evidence_items.claim: 1X discloses that NEO works autonomously by default for known/basic tasks, but for complex or unknown chores owners can schedule a 1X Expert to remotely supervise, and the product supports remote piloting through the mobile app and VR device.
evidence_items.notes: This is an official limitation disclosure and should be weighted more heavily than broad marketing autonomy language.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Separates task completion evidence from autonomous task execution evidence.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Official pages say NEO works autonomously by default, but unknown or complex chores can use scheduled 1X Expert guidance, and users can pilot NEO from the app and a VR device.
evidence_items.source_location: NEO product page Expert Mode and Utility sections; Order page Utility section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company disclosure; does not quantify how often Expert Mode is required.

evidence_items.title: Official factory and preorder-capacity update
evidence_items.claim: 1X says the NEO preorder campaign booked out the next year's production capacity in five days at 10,000 NEOs, the Hayward factory has commenced full-scale production, and current capacity is up to 10,000 NEOs per year with a plan to scale toward 100,000+ annually by the end of 2027.
evidence_items.notes: Stronger than a generic preorder page for production readiness, but still a company claim and not customer deployment proof.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Supports commercial traction/manufacturing readiness while preserving the gap to verified deliveries.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: 1X says it booked 10,000 NEOs in five days, started full-scale production at the 58,000 sq ft Hayward factory, employs 200+ there, and has capacity up to 10,000 units per year.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official factory update; no third-party production audit or customer delivery confirmation.

evidence_items.title: 1X world-model robot-policy results and caveats
evidence_items.claim: 1X reports that its 1XWM world-model policy is integrated into NEO and was evaluated on real-world tasks with 30 trials per task, showing some successful manipulation primitives but also difficult dexterous tasks with 0% success in the displayed chart and admitted depth/contact failure modes.
evidence_items.notes: Company-run technical result with useful caveats; not an independent benchmark.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Adds concrete autonomous manipulation evidence, but only within 1X's reported test setup.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: 1X describes a world-model policy trained with web video, egocentric human video, robot data, and an inverse dynamics model; it reports 30 trials per task and notes pouring/drawing failures plus weak 3D grounding cases.
evidence_items.source_location: 1X World Model | From Video to Action
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official technical blog; no raw logs or independent replication found.

evidence_items.title: Company mobility controller claims for stairs and floor poses
evidence_items.claim: 1X claims Redwood's RL mobility controller supports natural walking in any direction, sitting, standing, kneeling, getting up from the floor, and stair traversal using stereo RGB vision.
evidence_items.notes: Company-run mobility evidence; no independent fall-rate or obstacle benchmark.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Home biped mobility and stairs matter directly for household fit.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: 1X says its RL controller gives Redwood walking in any direction, sitting/standing/kneeling, floor recovery, and up/down stair traversal with stereo vision.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official technical blog and demo context; not independently measured.

demos.title: 1X NEO launch and hands-on demo context
observed_capabilities: Launch materials show household chores such as laundry, dishes, tidying, fetching, and turning off lights.
Official materials disclose Expert Mode for tasks NEO does not know and remote control through app/VR.
Media hands-on context reports heavy teleoperation dependence in demonstrated tasks.
demos.editing_notes: Not manually timestamp-reviewed in this update; treat as curated unless future review verifies continuity.
demos.teleoperation_notes: Official product/order pages disclose Expert Mode and remote-control capability; media coverage of WSJ hands-on testing says the demonstrated work was heavily teleoperated. Do not treat demo task completion as autonomous unless a segment explicitly says it is autonomous.
demos.environment: public company demo or reported demonstration
caveats: Demo evidence is not a sustained deployment or independent benchmark.
Expert Mode means task completion and autonomy must be scored separately.
No raw uninterrupted task-suite footage was reviewed.

observed_segments.observation: Company launch/product pages and media coverage show household chore scenarios, while official pages disclose Expert Mode/remote control and media reporting emphasizes teleoperation in hands-on testing.
observed_segments.verification_notes: Timestamp not verified; manual video review required before using as audit-grade timestamp evidence.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No independent household task benchmark, intervention rate, or fallback-to-Expert-Mode rate was found. Official claims say NEO has basic autonomy and grows over time, while official Expert Mode and media hands-on reporting show a material human-in-the-loop caveat.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Score autonomy conservatively; credit specific company-reported autonomous results only within their stated setup.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: 1X claims preorders, 2026 U.S. deliveries, factory production, and booked 10,000-unit next-year capacity, but no independently verified customer deliveries or in-home deployment metrics were found.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Credit commercial intent and manufacturing progress, not proven field deployment.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Official specs include soft body, no external pinch points, HIC <250, 4h runtime, tendon load-cycle claims, and factory reliability-lab cycle counts, but no independent safety certification, field uptime, fall-rate, service-rate, or warranty-return data was found.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Treat safety/reliability as design claims until third-party or customer field data appears.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Remote Expert Mode, cameras, microphones, app monitoring, and data collection create material in-home privacy questions; reviewed sources did not provide independent verification of privacy controls or operator access constraints.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Apply a human-interaction/accessibility caveat; do not treat remote assistance as pure product autonomy.

excluded_claims.reason: Reviewed sources do not independently verify broad autonomy.

excluded_claims.claim: Independent benchmark across all arena dimensions
excluded_claims.reason: No full independent benchmark was found.
Official sources support preorders, planned 2026 shipments, and production capacity, but reviewed sources did not independently confirm delivered customer homes or sustained operating metrics.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: 1X NEO is a preorder/purchasable home humanoid with unusually detailed official specs and production claims: 5'6", 66 lb, 75 total listed DoF, 22 DoF per hand, 18 lb per-arm payload, 4h runtime, Jetson Thor compute, stereo fisheye cameras, $20,000 Early Access ownership, $499/month subscription, and claimed 2026 U.S. deliveries. Stronger 2026 evidence adds factory production and company-run AI/mobility results, but the decisive caveat remains autonomy: official Expert Mode/remote-control disclosures and WSJ/media hands-on reporting mean household chore completion should not be credited as broad autonomous capability.
strongest_evidence: Official product/order pages provide concrete hardware specs, pricing, preorder terms, Expert Mode, remote control, and 2026 delivery claims.
1X's April 2026 factory update claims 10,000 booked NEOs, full-scale Hayward production, 200+ factory staff, and up to 10,000 units/year capacity.
1X technical posts report Redwood/1XWM autonomous manipulation and mobility work with explicit caveats and some measured task trials.
weakest_evidence: No independent household task benchmark, intervention-rate data, or customer field telemetry.
Hands-on/media evidence indicates heavy teleoperation dependence at launch-era demos.
No independently verified customer deliveries or sustained in-home deployment metrics.
known_do_not_credit: Broad autonomy beyond specific source context.
Teleoperated or Expert-assisted chore completion as autonomous execution.
Preorders/factory capacity as completed customer deployments.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Best scored as a serious preorder home humanoid with detailed official specs, manufacturing momentum, and company-run AI/mobility evidence, but still weak independent proof and major Expert Mode/teleoperation caveats.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official product/order pages now provide concrete specs: 5'6", 66 lb, 22 DoF per hand, 18 lb arm payload, 4h runtime, 842 Wh battery, stereo fisheye cameras, Jetson Thor compute, $20,000 ownership, and $499/month subscription.
Official factory update claims 10,000 booked NEOs, full-scale Hayward production, 200+ employees, and up to 10,000 units/year capacity.
